title: VibeThinker-3B: Frontier Reasoning in a Small Model
hook: A 3B model matches giant flagships on hard math and coding - because verifiable reasoning, it turns out, compresses into a tiny 'reasoning core.'
key_points: A 3B dense model scores 94.3 on AIME26 and 80.2 Pass@1 on LiveCodeBench v6, rivaling far larger flagship reasoning models.
Trained with a 'Spectrum-to-Signal' recipe: curriculum supervised fine-tuning, multi-domain RL, then offline self-distillation.
Parametric Compression-Coverage Hypothesis: verifiable reasoning compresses into a compact core, but broad world knowledge still needs many parameters.
Claim-level test-time scaling lifts AIME26 to 97.1; out-of-distribution transfer stays strong (96.1% on unseen LeetCode contests).
93.4 on IFEval shows the extreme reasoning tuning doesn't break instruction-following.
content_html: VibeThinker-3B is a 3-billion-parameter dense model built to probe how far verifiable reasoning can be pushed in a strictly small-model regime. Using a "Spectrum-to-Signal" post-training paradigm — curriculum-based supervised fine-tuning, multi-domain reinforcement learning, and offline self-distillation — its authors report frontier-level scores: 94.3 on AIME26 (97.1 with claim-level test-time scaling) and 80.2 Pass@1 on LiveCodeBench v6, matching or exceeding flagships orders of magnitude larger.
extra_html: The headline isn't just the benchmark numbers but the framing. The team proposes the Parametric Compression-Coverage Hypothesis: verifiable reasoning (math, code) seems to compress into a small "reasoning core," while open-domain knowledge and general competence require broad parameter coverage over facts and long-tail scenarios. A 93.4 on IFEval suggests the reasoning push doesn't sacrifice instruction-following. The takeaway, per the authors, is that compact models are a complementary route to frontier capability — not just a cheaper substitute. Results are the authors' own claims; see the technical report for methodology and caveats.

related.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning
related.hook: DeepSeek shows strong reasoning can emerge from RL on verifiable rewards with minimal supervised data - and those reasoning traces can be distilled into smaller models.

related.title: On the Geometry of On-Policy Distillation
related.hook: On-policy distillation isn't a midpoint between fine-tuning and RL — it carves its own narrow path through parameter space, locking into a low-dimensional subspace early in training.

related.title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute
related.hook: A new scaling axis: instead of a bigger model, let a model think longer at inference — often a better use of compute, and the principle behind o1 and R1.

prereqs.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting
prereqs.hook: Ask a big model to 'think step by step' and its math and logic scores jump. Reasoning was there all along — you just had to ask it to show its work.

flashcards.prompt: What is the Parametric Compression-Coverage Hypothesis?
flashcards.back_html: Verifiable reasoning can be compressed into a compact "reasoning core," so small models can be frontier reasoners — but broad open-domain knowledge and general competence still require wide parameter coverage.

flashcards.prompt: How does VibeThinker-3B reach frontier reasoning despite its tiny size?

choices.text: A post-training pipeline: curriculum SFT, multi-domain RL, then offline self-distillation
Pretraining on roughly 10x more tokens than larger models
A new attention mechanism that replaces the transformer

flashcards.explanation_html: VibeThinker-3B is a small dense model; its gains come from the "Spectrum-to-Signal" post-training recipe, not from more pretraining data or a new architecture.

flashcards.prompt: What does VibeThinker-3B suggest about the role of small models?
flashcards.back_html: They're not merely deployment-efficient substitutes — they're a complementary path to frontier-level performance in verifiable, parameter-dense capability regimes.
